To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) fault tolerance can be formalized in a logical framework and 2) fault tolerance analysis can be made independent of any particular fault assumption, by means of partial model checking techniques.

the logical characterization of fault-tolerance properties can be used to: (a) specify fault tolerance in an uniform and general way; (b) analyze fault tolerance in an open system context; (c) validate fault tolerance independently from any particular fault model.

- a logical characterization of the notion of fault tolerance is proposed; - this characterization is based on the use of the equational @mcalculus; - the analysis of a fault tolerance property is expressed as an analysis of the equational formula expressing such a property; - the analysis problem is independent from any particular assumption about faults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formalization of fault tolerance and the development of methods and tools for its analysis.

the proposed framework is a powerful tool for the formal specification and analysis of fault tolerant systems.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a general framework for a formal characterization and analysis of fault tolerance, based on partial model-checking strategies and on the use of the formalism of @m-calculus.
the proposed framework is a general and flexible tool for the analysis of fault tolerant systems, which can be applied in many different situations and for a wide range of systems.

we have proposed a formal characterization of fault tolerant systems and we have provided the theoretical basis and the practical tools for the verification of fault tolerance in a wide range of systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a uniform and formal framework is possible for the logical specification and analysis of fault tolerance.
the logical characterization of fault-tolerance can be a powerful and flexible tool to analyze fault tolerant systems.
